description:
This 2007 Dodge Dakota SLT Quad Cab is a mid-size pickup with four full doors and seating for passengers in both rows. Its size places it between a compact truck and a full-size model, which gives it a familiar driving position and usable interior space without moving into the larger footprint of a heavier-duty truck. The cab design provides straightforward access to the rear area, and the SLT trim identifies it as a well-equipped version of the Dakota line. The body style is practical for daily use, while still leaving the open cargo bed available for hauling tasks that fit within a truck of this class.

This Dakota includes Power Seats, which allow the driver to adjust seating position with built-in controls rather than manual levers. That equipment can make it easier to fine-tune comfort and reach behind the wheel, especially when the vehicle is shared by different drivers. The interior is arranged for regular use, with controls placed in a conventional manner and trim that reflects the truck's intended role as a work-capable vehicle with added convenience features. The Quad Cab format also gives the cabin a more flexible feel than a regular cab, with rear seating available for additional occupants or for carrying items inside the vehicle when needed.

This truck also comes with Fog Lights, Satellite Radio Ready, and Keyless Entry. The fog lights are mounted to provide additional forward lighting equipment beyond the standard headlamps. Satellite radio readiness means the audio system is prepared for that service, subject to activation and any required subscription. Keyless entry adds remote access for the doors, which is a useful everyday feature when getting in and out of the vehicle repeatedly. These items add convenience and utility without changing the basic character of the truck, and they fit with the rest of the equipment in a simple, functional way.

This 2007 Dodge Dakota SLT Quad Cab sits in a segment known for balancing passenger space with truck utility, and this example keeps that approach clear through its cabin size and available features. The interior offers the expected seating positions for a four-door pickup, while the power-adjustable seat adds an element of driver convenience that is often appreciated in routine use. The presence of fog lights, keyless entry, and satellite radio readiness gives it a useful set of equipment for commuting, errands, or light-duty hauling. This Dakota presents its equipment plainly, with the details centered on what it has rather than on any interpretation of how it might be used.

  • Lane departure prevention - Keep it between the lines. It only takes a moment of inattention for your vehicle to drift.   • Forward collision mitigation - Forward thinking. You look away for just a second and suddenly the vehicle in front of you has stopped. That's when the forward collision mitigation system comes to life. When it senses an impending impact, it will activate a combination of features to help prevent or reduce the severity of an accident. Forward collision mitigation is always looking ahead.
  • Pedestrian impact prevention - An extra step toward safety. Pedestrians don't always stop, look, and listen, but with Pedestrian Impact Prevention, your vehicle is equipped to better see them and avoid them. This system constantly monitors the road ahead to identify and track pedestrians. It projects that image to an interior display screen, AND should an impact become likely, Pedestrian impact prevention takes steps to avoid a collision.
  • Hands-on cruise control. Set it and forget it. Road trips used to be stressful. Cruise control only managed speed, but not distance or safety.
